capabilities: Restore the saved reading position when reopening Markdown and PDF files
Show reading progress in the status bar as percentage, lines, or pages
Add, open, remove, or reset one quick bookmark per file from the status bar or command palette
Highlight the bookmarked Markdown paragraph or PDF page
Configure completion threshold, automatic resume, and duplicate-tab behavior
disambiguation: Not a general bookmark manager; each file gets only one quick bookmark, alongside the saved reading position.
extras: Desktop only (macOS, Windows, Linux); verified on macOS with Obsidian 1.12.7 and Windows/Linux testing is still welcome. PDF page restore relies on internal PDF.js elements, so Obsidian or PDF++ updates may temporarily break it. State is stored locally in the plugin's data.json and note content is never modified; debug logging is off by default.
problem: Obsidian does not remember where you stopped reading a long Markdown note or PDF, so reopening a file means manually finding your place again.

relations.evidence: Works with Obsidian's built-in PDF viewer and is designed to coexist with PDF++.

summary: Reading tracker that records where you stopped in Markdown and PDF files, restores that position on reopen, and keeps one quick bookmark per file.
